title: A Safehouse for the Deadline
premise: Private security contractor August Galloway receives a calendar invitation from her handler, Marcus Vey, dated for tomorrow—the same day his body washed out of the Rotterdam canals. The invitation leads her to a decommissioned NATO safehouse where Vey cached evidence that three governments laundered a black-site program through the very contracts August has spent years quietly burying. Hunted by a state assassin known only as Lark and betrayed by the firm that trained her, August assembles an unlikely crew: a retired archivist, a disgraced interpreter, and the teenage daughter Vey never told her he had. In the end, August chooses exposure over survival, releasing the archive through the girl's hands while she draws Lark into the safehouse's collapsing tunnels, buying the truth its daylight at nearly the cost of her own life.
about_author: Coral Kavanagh is a former maritime insurance investigator who spent a decade reconstructing cargo histories that companies preferred forgotten. She writes thrillers from a houseboat in Ghent, where she claims the best plots arrive with the fog.

chapters.title: Invitation from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: August Galloway finishes a forgettable protection job in Antwerp when her phone pings: a meeting request from Marcus Vey, her handler, for tomorrow at 09:00—sent after his confirmed death. POV August. The emotional beat is cold professional unease cracking into genuine grief she refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Safehouse Clause
chapters.summary: August follows the invitation's coordinates to a shuttered NATO safehouse in the Ardennes and finds Vey's dead-drop: a drive documenting how three governments funneled a black-site program through contracts she herself helped sanitize. POV August. Beat: the sick vertigo of realizing her own invisible work was load-bearing for something monstrous.

chapters.title: Lark at the Window
chapters.summary: A state assassin called Lark breaches the safehouse; August escapes through the tunnel network but learns the firm that trained her has sold her location. POV August, with an intercut of Lark's methodical, almost tender professionalism. Beat: the hunter's calm versus August's first taste of being prey.

chapters.title: What Vey Kept
chapters.summary: Decoding the drive, August discovers Vey's personal files: photographs, a birth certificate, and a name—Noor, a fourteen-year-old in a Rotterdam foster home who is his daughter, and his designated heir for the archive. POV August. Beat: grief sharpening into purpose; the dead man had a plan and a family she never knew he had.

chapters.title: The Girl with the Inheritance
chapters.summary: August extracts Noor from Rotterdam as Lark's surveillance tightens; the girl is sharp, hostile, and already halfway to decoding her father's cipher games. POV August, with Noor's diary fragments. Beat: two orphans of the same man circling each other, trust built one grudging truth at a time.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Door
chapters.summary: August calls in favors from her found family—a retired archivist named Osei and disgraced interpreter Mirela—who confirm the archive is authentic but warn that every official channel leads back to the program. POV Mirela. Beat: the claustrophobia of realizing the system itself is the locked door, and loyalty is the only key.

chapters.title: The Firm's Quiet Offer
chapters.summary: August's old employer offers her life, money, and erasure in exchange for the drive; she stalls them while Osei copies the archive and Mirela maps a press handoff through an exiled journalist. POV August. Beat: temptation as threat—the comfortable lie offered back to her in her own voice.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Fog
chapters.summary: The handoff is ambushed; Mirela is taken and Osei wounded, and August learns the leak was Vey's own old contact, coerced years ago. Noor decrypts Vey's final message: a backup route through the safehouse tunnels, meant for exactly this night. POV Noor. Beat: despair transmuted into inheritance—the dead handler still protecting them.

chapters.title: Deadline at the Safehouse
chapters.summary: Climax. August releases the archive through Noor and the journalist while luring Lark into the collapsing tunnel network beneath the safehouse; Mirela is traded free, Osei's copy goes live, and August barely survives the collapse as Lark is buried by the program's own architecture. POV August. Beat: sacrifice without martyrdom—she chooses the truth over the exit.

chapters.title: A Safehouse for the Living
chapters.summary: Weeks later, inquiries open in three capitals while August, healing and officially nonexistent, shares a rented house by the sea with Noor, Mirela, and Osei. Vey's last file contains a photo of all of them, taken years ago by a lens he never explained. POV August. Beat: found family as the true inheritance; memory as the only safehouse that holds.
